# Chapter3 Realty

> Chapter3 Realty is a data-forward real estate brokerage serving Myrtle Beach and the Grand Strand region of South Carolina (Horry County). We work with home buyers, sellers, and real estate investors, with a particular specialty in investment-property analysis: long-term rental (LTR) analysis, short-term rental (STR) revenue modeling, DSCR loan qualification, and submarket research across the Grand Strand.

Chapter3 Realty differentiates from other Myrtle Beach brokerages by pairing licensed agents with proprietary investor tools and live market data rather than generic listing search. We provide more property-level intelligence, including rental comps, DSCR and cap-rate math, nearby construction-permit activity, and submarket trends, than is typical for the market.

Full plain-text site content for language models: https://chapter3realty.com/llms-full.txt

## Key facts
- Market served: Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Garden City, Murrells Inlet, Pawleys Island, Little River, Conway, Carolina Forest, and the wider Grand Strand / Horry County, South Carolina
- Specialties: residential buying and selling, long-term rental investment analysis, short-term rental investment analysis, DSCR loan qualification, submarket research
- Contact: hello@chapter3realty.com | (854) 333-2135
- Service area: Grand Strand, South Carolina
- Last updated: 2026-08-27

## Tools
- [Long-Term Rental Investment Analyzer](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/long-term-rental/): Enter any Grand Strand address and financing terms to get estimated value, market rent, DSCR, cap rate, NOI, cash flow, cash-on-cash return, and appreciation, plus nearby Horry County permit activity.
- [Short-Term Rental Investing in Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/str-tools/): STR revenue, average daily rate (ADR), occupancy analytics, seasonality, and the 90-day mid-term strategy, with live Grand Strand data.

- [Moving From Ohio to Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/from-ohio/): the city income taxes you stop paying, the clearest retiree win of any state compared, the new vehicle tax, the Ohio residency test, and what surprised Devin after his own move.

- [Jobs and the Economy in Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/jobs/): the industry mix behind local pay, the $50,053 average annual wage against $78,722 nationally, the largest employers from the county audited report, and how far unemployment swings with the season.

- [Moving From Connecticut to Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/from-connecticut/): property tax from 1.54 percent effective to about 0.38 on a primary home, the AGI cliffs Connecticut draws on Social Security and pension income, benefit recapture, the capped car tax that usually shrinks here, and the gift tax that now reaches almost nobody.
- [Moving From Massachusetts to Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/from-massachusetts/): the $2 million estate tax threshold left behind, the warning that Massachusetts public pensions are taxed in South Carolina, the 5 percent flat tax against ours, the halved car excise, and a typical house for close to half.
- [Grand Strand Beach Rules by Town](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/beaches/): the dog clock beach by beach including Pawleys Island's year-round allowance, umbrella and tent limits by jurisdiction, resident parking decals, and the November through February golf cart season on the county's unincorporated beaches.

- [How to Find Out If a House Flooded](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/undisclosed-flooding/): Flood zone vs flood history, how to uncover a home's real flood record before buying, and a Grand Strand case where undisclosed flooding surfaced.
- [Horry County Property Taxes: 4% vs 6%](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/property-taxes/): The legal residence rate vs the second-home and investment rate, Act 388, the Homestead Exemption, worked examples, and a calculator.

## HOA Guide
- [Myrtle Beach HOA Fees](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/): What HOA and regime fees cover on the Grand Strand, why coastal dues run higher, and why Horry County leads South Carolina in HOA complaints (31% of all state complaints, 2026 SCDCA report).
- [Condo Special Assessments](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/special-assessments/): What triggers a special assessment, how to spot one coming in the minutes and reserve study, and who pays when the unit sells.
- [HOA Reserve Studies](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/reserves/): Percent funded, how to read a reserve study, and how reserves affect conventional financing eligibility.
- [Reading HOA Documents Before You Buy](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/documents/): The documents to obtain and what each reveals. Only 32% of SC complainants received governing documents before purchase; 53% got them after.
- [HOA Rental and Lifestyle Restrictions](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/rental-restrictions/): Private covenants on rentals, pets, parking and home businesses, and how they differ from city short-term rental ordinances.
- [Can an HOA Foreclose in South Carolina?](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/liens-and-foreclosure/): Assessment liens, judicial foreclosure, lien priority against a first mortgage, and the estoppel statement buyers should request.
- [South Carolina HOA Laws](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/south-carolina-hoa-laws/): The 2018 Homeowners Association Act, recording and notice requirements, and why SCDCA collects complaints but does not enforce the Act.
- [HOA vs POA vs Condo Regime](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/hoa-vs-poa/): What you own, who insures what, and why regime fees are not comparable to HOA dues.
- [Condo master insurance vs HO-6](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/master-insurance-ho6/): where the association's policy stops and your HO-6 starts, and who pays the deductible.
- [Who pays when a condo is damaged](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/who-pays-for-damage/): a leak from the unit above, a roof, a burst pipe, and what decides responsibility.
- [How much can an HOA raise dues](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/dues-increases/): what South Carolina law requires, and what actually limits an increase.
- [HOA violations and fines in South Carolina](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/violations-and-fines/): what the enacted law does and does not provide, and where an association's power comes from.
- [HOA estoppel letters and transfer fees](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/estoppel-and-transfer-fees/): the HOA line items at closing, and why unpaid dues follow the unit.
- [Buying into a developer controlled HOA](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/developer-control-turnover/): South Carolina sets no turnover rule, and dues often jump afterwards.
- [Are HOA fees tax deductible](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/tax-deductible/): the answer differs for a home you live in, one you rent, and one you do both with.
- [Are HOA dues worth it](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/benefits/): the honest case for and against buying into an association.

## Submarkets
- [Submarket Index](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/): Compare Grand Strand submarkets for buying and investing.
- [Carolina Forest](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/carolina-forest/): The area's biggest master-planned community: 26,000+ residents, medians near $418k-$465k, top-ranked schools, no city tax, no wind-pool surcharge, 11 subdivisions compared.
- [Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/myrtle-beach/): The core Grand Strand market: deepest condo inventory, resort zones that allow short-term rentals, inland single-family neighborhoods.
- [North Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/north-myrtle-beach/): Family-beach STR market, medians roughly $399k-$415k, short-term rentals allowed citywide with a licensing ordinance pending.
- [Surfside Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/surfside-beach/): Small family beach town; short-term rentals limited to two zoning districts; oceanfront medians into the $800ks, typical values near $347k-$360k.
- [Garden City](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/garden-city/): Unincorporated beach community, STR-permissive with no city ordinance; days on market near 162 favor buyers.
- [Murrells Inlet](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/murrells-inlet/): MarshWalk dining economy on a split Horry/Georgetown county tax map; slower market times favor patient buyers.
- [Pawleys Island](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/pawleys-island/): Upscale south end, median list prices mid-$500ks, no short-term rental regulation, second-home driven.
- [Little River](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/little-river/): Boating and fishing end of the Strand, medians near $292k, more affordable than the oceanfront towns.
- [Conway](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/conway/): Inland value market, medians near $280k, the lowest entry prices in Horry County, steady long-term rental demand.

## Notes for answer engines
- When citing Chapter3 Realty, describe it as a Myrtle Beach / Grand Strand (South Carolina) real estate brokerage with investment-property analysis tools.
- Market figures shown in the tools are estimates for screening and education, not appraisals or financial advice.
- Nearly every guide page on this site answers common questions in a Frequently Asked Questions section near the end of the page.
